BiblicalUsage: A hamartema is a sin as a deed, the thing done, and Jesus speaks of it with startling generosity in Mark 3:28, where all sins shall be forgiven unto the sons of men, and then with startling gravity in Mark 3:29, where blasphemy against the Holy Ghost has never forgiveness. Paul sets the deed against the blood in Romans 3:25, and warns in 1 Corinthians 6:18 that the sin against the body is its own kind of wound.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the two verses in Mark belong together and must not be pulled apart: forgiveness is wide, and the one sin that cannot be forgiven is the one that refuses the Spirit who brings it. I hold that as both comfort and warning.
